item.title: Lilly Zepbound/Foundayo Weight Loss Maintenance
item.description:
• Summary: Eli Lilly presented data showing that its drugs Zepbound and Foundayo effectively help patients maintain weight loss after switching from other treatments. The findings reinforce Lilly's leadership in the obesity market and offer new maintenance options for patients.
  • MoAs: Zepbound (tirzepatide): GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist; Foundayo: mechanism not disclosed in available sources.
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, BioSpace, Endpoints News

item.title: Novo Nordisk and Lilly GLP-1 Data
item.description:
• Summary: Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly touted early response and weight-loss maintenance data for their respective GLP-1-based therapies at the ECO 2026 congress. Novo's deal with Lexicon and its diabetes ambitions were also highlighted, along with discussions on body composition effects of CagriSema (cagrilintide + semaglutide).
  • MoAs: Semaglutide: GLP-1 receptor agonist; Tirzepatide: GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist; Cagrilintide: amylin analog; CagriSema: combination of cagrilintide and semaglutide.
  • Sources: Fierce Biotech, Fierce Pharma, Pharmaceutical Technology

item.title: Liver Disease MetALD Series
item.description:
• Summary: Part 3 of the STAT series on liver disease examines MetALD (metabolic and alcohol-related liver disease), focusing on the deadliest drug involved and its impact on public health.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: STAT News

item.title: UAE Approves AstraZeneca Baxfendy
item.description:
• Summary: The United Arab Emirates has approved AstraZeneca's Baxfendy for the treatment of hypertension. Baxfendy is a new combination therapy that offers an additional option for blood pressure management.
  • MoAs: Combination of an angiotensin receptor blocker (ARB) and a calcium channel blocker (CCB), exerting antihypertensive effects via vasodilation and reduced peripheral resistance.
  • Sources: Pharmaceutical Technology
